890: (17) It is forbidden to place cold water {on the meicham,} even to thaw it, whenever the meicham is so hot that if one placed it there it would reach yad soledes bo — for it is like placing opposite the fire. {Rama: And if the meicham is not hot enough for this, it is permitted even for something not cooked at all.}
893: (108) 'It is forbidden to place it cold, etc.' — based on what the Rama concluded above in seif 15 in the gloss, this should be lenient if it was a cooked item and had not completely cooled.
895: (109) 'A lot' — we are concerned lest he forget and leave it there until it is cooked.
897: (110) 'Like placing, etc.' — meaning and as explained above in seif 14 that even to remove its chill it is forbidden if it can come to cooking.
899: (111) 'And if it is not, etc.' — and if the meicham is standing on the fire, see above in seif 8.
901: (112) 'Permitted' — even if the cold item is something that has never been cooked.
903: (101) 'The hand is scalded in it' — therefore it is forbidden to place cold water on a hot plate so that it thaws, because if it stays there for a long time it may reach yad soledes bo.
905: (102) 'Opposite the fire' — similar to the decree we saw in seif 14.
907: (103) 'Is not that hot' — the meicham is not hot enough that there is a concern that the water placed on it will reach yad soledes bo.
